summary: A 220-second, eight-act brief grounded in the retained manuscript and numerical checks.
content:
Create A FRONTIER FOR THE ZEROS for learners comfortable with algebra, graphs and complex coordinates, without assuming analytic number theory. Central question: how can arithmetic estimates exclude zeros beyond a fixed frontier while leaving RH open? Learners should explain the prime–zero connection, distinguish Quasi-RH from RH, and understand the reciprocal-pole contradiction.

Prerequisite graph: primes → Euler product → analytic continuation → zeros → critical strip/frontier; local zero → winding → reciprocal pole; Eisenstein arithmetic → reflection/Poisson comparisons → common power saving → holomorphic continuation → contradiction.

Define terms when introduced: \(s=\sigma+it\); zero \(\zeta(\rho)=0\); pole; analytic continuation; critical strip/line; fixed zero-free half-plane; characters as multiplicative arithmetic weights; finite-order Hecke family over \(F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})\); winding number; holomorphic as complex analytic. Later define \(\eta\) as target character, \(Z\) as positive scale, \(J_\eta\) as normalized arithmetic sum, and \(f_\eta\) as reciprocal-L Mellin signal. Define \(\beta_*\) as the supremum of \(1/2\) and real parts of primitive Hecke-family zeros in \([1/2,1]\); it need not be attained.

Eight connected acts, including transitions and reading pauses:

1. 0–24s: Fly through an actual numerical zeta valley toward the first known zero. Immediately identify analytic continuation and the sampled height \(h=\log(1+|\zeta(s)|)\). Define a zero. Label the landscape a visualization of function values.
2. 24–46s: Prime-factor ribs resolve into complex geometry. Present \(\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-s}=\prod_p(1-p^{-s})^{-1}\), visibly restricted to \(\Re(s)>1\). Explain continuation into the strip.
3. 46–76s: Extrude the critical strip around a gold \(\sigma=1/2\) spine. Fix sampled known zeros at the four supplied full-precision ordinates. Distinguish RH from a fixed frontier. Move the boundary \(11/12\to7/8\), then reveal its zeta-symmetric \(1/8\) partner. Leave the closed central strip unresolved. Finite windows illustrate an assertion at every height.
4. 76–108s: Orbit two tilted complex planes. A positively oriented radius-0.1 circle around the first sampled zero and its computed zeta image carry synchronized points. Explain one winding and \(\zeta(s)\approx\zeta'(\rho)(s-\rho)\). Reveal a labeled capped reciprocal spike. Simplicity applies to this sample.
5. 108–134s: Travel through the Eisenstein triangular lattice into a labeled proof map. Reflection bounds the completed cubic-theta sum; Poisson isolates the principal reciprocal-L signal and remaining character rows. Explain why the Hecke family is necessary even for zeta.
6. 134–156s: Refine the sculpture: Part II changes the normalized sum through prime compensation, unequal scales, inverse second moments and plain-polynomial fourth moments. Sequentially reveal \(C(s)=s-11/16\) and \(C(7/8)=3/16\).
7. 156–202s: Assume \(\beta_*>\sigma_0=7/8\). Begin with “small sum + small difference ⇒ small signal.” Sequentially reveal \(|J_\eta(Z)|\ll_\eta Z^{C(\sigma_0)+\omega}\), \(|J_\eta(Z)-f_\eta(Z)|\ll_\eta Z^{C(\beta_*)-\sigma}\), and \(\epsilon_*=\min(\beta_*-\sigma_0-\omega,\sigma)>0\). Define this \(\sigma\) as a saving exponent. Exponents are common across targets; constants may depend on them. Power saving and rapid decay at zero yield Mellin holomorphy for \(\Re(s)>\beta_*-\epsilon_*\). Fourier inversion, identity and \(|H_\eta|\ge1/2\) continue the reciprocal. The supremum supplies some hypothetical zero inside: its reciprocal pole contradicts holomorphy. Label this conditional proof schematic.
8. 202–220s: Return to the landscape and fixed curtains. Attribute the strict, uniform \(\Re(s)>7/8\) assertion for zeta, every Dirichlet L-function and finite-order Hecke L-functions over F to the manuscript. Allow principal poles at \(s=1\). State RH remains open. End: “OpenAI manuscript / 30 September 2026 / family 003. Explains the manuscript; full proof and Lean build not independently checked.”

Acceptance: distinguish numerical illustration, local topology and the manuscript’s argument. Never move known zeros, assert boundary nonvanishing, infer a magnitude lower bound, fabricate character data or erase poles by cancellation. Exclude the pole from numerical meshes. Full proof reconstruction and later applications are outside scope.

Every mathematical shot uses genuine 3D space: large illuminated meshes, deliberate occlusion, silhouettes, parallax and motivated closeups. Preserve bone #F3EFE6, ink #202A35, teal #176B72, coral #C76F51 and gold #AD8542. Reserve readable bands: one main MathTex formula and two short lines maximum; replace captions and hold dense formulas at least six seconds. Deliver 210–230 seconds at 1080p/60fps. AstraFilm uses CE 0.19 Cairo, move_camera/set_camera_orientation, only manim/numpy/math, precomputed modest meshes/paths, and no external assets or I/O. Require independent numerical checks, zero residuals below 10⁻¹⁰ and winding approximately one.
checks: Read retained manuscript introduction, Proposition 2.1, Part II normalization, Section 20 and formalization scope.
Euler–Maclaurin N=64/eight corrections: four zero residuals ≤1.20×10⁻¹⁴; 48-point comparison against N=96/ten corrections differed ≤5.64×10⁻¹⁴. Computed 512-segment loop winding: 1.0000000000000002.
Act timings total 220 seconds. Local renderer contract inspected; Manim/mpmath unavailable in checked environments, so API and mpmath validation remain pending. No edits or rendering performed.
